steps.tx: The historic **Dallas criteria** defines myocarditis by inflammatory cellular infiltrates with adjacent myocyte necrosis on **endomyocardial biopsy**, though sampling error is common due to patchy involvement. Biopsy remains the diagnostic reference standard, particularly in unexplained acute fulminant heart failure or refractory ventricular arrhythmias.

rows: Absence of inflammation with reparative fibrosis

steps.tx: Updated **Lake Louise Criteria** for **cardiac MRI** diagnosis of myocarditis requires at least **1** T1-based criterion for myocardial injury and at least 1 T**2**-based criterion for myocardial edema. Meeting both criteria achieves high sensitivity and specificity, noninvasively confirming active myocardial inflammation. Comprehensive clinical evaluation requires careful correlation with serial electrocardiographic tracings and hemodynamic parameters.

left.title: T1-Based Criteria (Myocardial Injury)
points: Elevated native myocardial T1 relaxation time
Subepicardial or mid-wall late gadolinium enhancement
Reflects active necrosis, hyperemia, or fibrosis

right.title: T2-Based Criteria (Myocardial Edema)
points: Elevated native myocardial T2 relaxation time
Regional or global hyperintensity on T2-weighted images
Elevated T2 signal intensity ratio vs skeletal muscle

steps.tx: Panel A shows bright lateral wall signal on T2 imaging, marking **myocardial edema** from active inflammation. Panel B shows outer wall contrast uptake with a spared inner layer, called **subepicardial enhancement**, while the **subendocardium** stays dark. Together the paired T2 and T1 findings meet criteria for myocarditis and argue against blocked artery injury.
steps.say: This MRI pairs T2 images showing lateral wall swelling with contrast images showing outer layer scarring that spares the inner layer. That combination outside the coronary pattern points to inflammatory injury rather than infarction.

vis.alt: Short axis cardiac MRI pairs T2 weighted oedema images with contrast images showing subepicardial enhancement sparing the subendocardium.
vis.caption: Myocarditis MRI with lateral oedema and non ischaemic outer wall injury Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Fulminant myocarditis** presents with rapid onset cardiogenic shock requiring inotropic support or temporary **mechanical circulatory support** such as VA-ECMO or Impella, yet carries excellent long-term recovery if patients survive the acute phase. In contrast, subacute myocarditis frequently progresses silently to dilated cardiomyopathy.

left.title: Fulminant Myocarditis
points: Sudden acute cardiovascular collapse within 2 weeks
Severe hemodynamic compromise requiring mechanical support
Severe systolic dysfunction with normal LV cavity size
Excellent long-term LV ejection fraction recovery (> 85%)

right.title: Subacute / Chronic Myocarditis
points: Insidious onset over months to years
Frequently progresses irreversibly to dilated cardiomyopathy

steps.tx: **Giant cell myocarditis** is a rapidly fatal autoimmune disorder characterized by widespread **multinucleated giant cells** and extensive cardiomyocyte necrosis, presenting with refractory ventricular tachycardia and heart block requiring urgent combined immunosuppression. Early histological recognition on endomyocardial biopsy is imperative to initiate high-dose steroids and calcineurin inhibitors.

nodes.label: Young Patient with Rapid Shock, VT, or Complete Heart Block
Multinucleated Giant Cells + Myocyte Necrosis (No Granulomas)
Triple Immunosuppression: Steroids + Calcineurin Inhibitor + ATG

steps.tx: The micrograph shows **multinucleated giant cells** as large pink cells ringed by dense blue inflammatory infiltrate with fragmented **necrotic cardiomyocytes** at the edge. The callout links this pattern to **urgent combined immunosuppression** for VT and heart block. Recognizing giant cells matters because this form kills quickly without high dose steroids and calcineurin drugs started at once.
steps.say: This biopsy shows giant cell myocarditis, a fast and deadly heart inflammation. Huge cells with many nuclei sit among dense immune cells while nearby muscle fibers break apart. Because rhythm collapse and block can follow rapidly, this picture demands urgent combined immune suppression without delay.

vis.alt: Pink muscle biopsy shows huge multinucleated cells amid dense inflammation with dying muscle fibers labeled.
vis.caption: Microscopy with giant cells among inflamed muscle, Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Cardiac sarcoidosis** demonstrates patchy non-caseating granulomas with high affinity for the basal interventricular septum, diagnosed by **18F-FDG PET** and cardiac MRI, manifesting as high-grade AV block and ventricular arrhythmias. Focal hypermetabolic myocardial tracer uptake on **18**F-FDG PET differentiates active granulomatous inflammation from inactive scar tissue.

rows: Focal or focal-on-diffuse hypermetabolic myocardial uptake
Mid-wall or subepicardial LGE in basal septum
Definitive histology (modest yield < 25% due to patchiness)

steps.tx: **Immune checkpoint inhibitor** myocarditis carries mortality up to 50%, requiring immediate discontinuation of therapy and high-dose intravenous **methylprednisolone** at **1000** mg daily for **3** days followed by abatacept if refractory. Life-threatening conduction block can develop precipitously within the first **1** to 3 months of immunotherapy.

Life-threatening conduction block can develop precipitously within the first 1 to 3 months of immunotherapy.

nodes.label: Suspected ICI Myocarditis: Elevated Troponin or New AV Block
Immediate Permanent Discontinuation of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor
Pulse IV Methylprednisolone 1000 mg Daily for 3 Days
If Refractory at 48h: Add Abatacept (CTLA-4 Agonist) or Alemtuzumab

steps.tx: **Eosinophilic myocarditis** includes hypersensitivity myocarditis and hypereosinophilic syndrome or **Loeffler endocarditis**, characterized by endomyocardial fibrosis and apical thrombus formation with restrictive cardiomyopathy. Eosinophil degranulation releases major basic protein and eosinophil cationic protein, directly damaging endocardial structures and adjacent microvasculature throughout both ventricles.

rows: Intense eosinophilic infiltration and myocyte lysis
Chest pain, fever, acute heart failure
Endocardial thrombus layered along ventricular apex
Severe restrictive cardiomyopathy and valve regurgitation

steps.tx: **Takotsubo cardiomyopathy** is characterized by transient left ventricular **apical ballooning** triggered by intense emotional or physical stress with catecholamine surge, mimicking STEMI without obstructive coronary disease. Spontaneous recovery of left ventricular ejection fraction typically occurs over several weeks with supportive care. Comprehensive clinical evaluation requires careful correlation with serial electrocardiographic tracings and hemodynamic parameters.
